arml-2002-superrelay-01.title: List the divisors
arml-2002-superrelay-01.body:
The two-digit divisors are $11$, $13$, $2\cdot7=14$, $2\cdot11=22$, $2\cdot13=26$, $7\cdot11=77$, $7\cdot13=91$ ($2\cdot7\cdot11=154$ and larger are three-digit; $7,2$ are one-digit; $11\cdot13=143$ is three-digit). That is $7$.

**Answer: 7**

arml-2002-superrelay-02.title: Right triangle
arml-2002-superrelay-02.body:
$K=9$. Let the three congruent circles have radius $r$. Circle $Q$ is concentric with the large circle (center $O=Q$) and tangent to $P$ and $R$, so $OP=2r$; circle $P$ is tangent to the large circle from inside, so $OP=K-r$. Hence $K-r=2r$, $r=\frac K3=3$. The chord $AB$ is tangent to circle $Q$, so its distance from $O$ is $r=3$. With $M$ the midpoint of $AB$, right triangle $OMB$ gives $\left(\frac{AB}2\right)^2=9^2-3^2=72$, so $AB=2\sqrt{72}=12\sqrt2$.

*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $7$.)*

**Answer: $12\sqrt2$**

arml-2002-superrelay-03.title: Two equations
arml-2002-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $12\sqrt2$.)* $a^2+b^2=T^2$ and $a^2+4b^2=T^2+96$. Subtracting, $3b^2=96$, $b^2=32$, so $a^2=T^2-32=288-32=256$ and $|a|=16$.

**Answer: 16**

arml-2002-superrelay-04.title: $ABCD$ is a rhombus
arml-2002-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $16$.)* $ABCD$ is a rhombus whose diagonals are $BD=T$ (the difference of the bases, from the arrangement) and $AC=2h$, twice the height of a trapezoid. Its area is $\frac12\cdot AC\cdot BD=\frac12(2h)(T)=hT$. Setting $hT=(20.02)T$ gives $h=20.02$ (the value of $T$ cancels).

**Answer: 20.02**

arml-2002-superrelay-05.title: Condition on the first marble
arml-2002-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $20.02$.)* $K=20$. After the first marble is drawn, $19$ remain and $10$ of them have the other color, so the probability is $\dfrac{10}{19}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{10}{19}$**

arml-2002-superrelay-06.title: Geometric series in base 9
arml-2002-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the relay, the fraction $\frac{10}{19}$ came from the previous problem, so $T=D-N=19-10=9$.)* $.\overline A_9=\dfrac A9+\dfrac A{9^2}+\dots=\dfrac{A}{8}$. The equation $\dfrac A8=1-\dfrac A8$ gives $A=4$ (in general $A=\frac{T-1}2$).

**Answer: 4**

arml-2002-superrelay-07.title: Factor
arml-2002-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $4$.)* $K=7$ and $K^{2004}+3K^{2002}+2K^{2000}=K^{2000}\left(K^4+3K^2+2\right)=K^{2000}(K^2+1)(K^2+2)=7^{2000}\cdot50\cdot51=7^{2000}\cdot2\cdot5^2\cdot3\cdot17$. The largest prime factor is $17$.

**Answer: 17**

arml-2002-superrelay-08.title: Inclusion-exclusion
arml-2002-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the relay, the two numbers $m=11$ and $n=17$ were the answers passed from problems 9 and 7.)* If $A$ and $B$ overlap partially, $V(A)+V(B)-m=n$, so $V(A)+V(B)=28$; since $V(A)\ge V(B)$, $V(A)\ge14$. If $B$ lies inside $A$ (so $C=B$), then $V(B)=m=11$ and $V(A)=n=17$. Also $V(A)\le n=17$ always. So $14\le V(A)\le17$, and each of $14,15,16,17$ is possible ($V(B)=14,13,12,11$, all at least $m=11$). The number of possible volumes is $4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-2002-superrelay-09.title: Size of $\log T^3$
arml-2002-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $87$.)* $\log T^3=3\log87\approx3(1.9395)=5.82$, so $\lfloor\log T^3\rfloor=5$ and the value is $6+5=11$. (Check: $87^3=658503$ has six digits.)

**Answer: 11**

arml-2002-superrelay-10.title: Cofunction identity
arml-2002-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $160$.)* $K=32$. Write $\cos\frac\theta6=\sin\left(90^\circ-\frac\theta6\right)$. Then either $\frac\theta2+K=90-\frac\theta6$, giving $\frac{2\theta}3=90-K=58$ and $\theta=87$; or $\frac\theta2+K=180-\left(90-\frac\theta6\right)=90+\frac\theta6$, giving $\frac\theta3=90-K=58$ and $\theta=174^\circ$, which is not acute. So $\theta=87$.

**Answer: 87**

arml-2002-superrelay-11.title: Multiply the choices
arml-2002-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $2$.)* Entree: $4$ choices. Dessert: $3+1=4$ (including none). Salad or appetizer or nothing: $5+2T+1=10$ (a salad with a dressing counts as $2\cdot T=4$ choices). Total $4\cdot4\cdot10=160$.

**Answer: 160**

arml-2002-superrelay-12.title: Proportional equations
arml-2002-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $-7$.)* With $T=-7$ the first equation is $x-7y+5z=-1$ and the second is $-2x+14y-10z=K$, i.e. $x-7y+5z=-\frac K2$. These two planes are parallel, so the system has no solution unless they coincide: $-\frac K2=-1$, $K=2$ — and then there are infinitely many solutions. (For every other $K$ there are no solutions.)

**Answer: 2**

arml-2002-superrelay-13.title: Mean of consecutive integers
arml-2002-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $100+30\sqrt2$, so $b=30$.)* The mean of $b$ consecutive integers $n,n+1,\dots,n+b-1$ is $n+\frac{b-1}2=\frac{15}2$, so $n=\frac{16-b}2=\frac{16-30}2=-7$.

**Answer: $-7$**

arml-2002-superrelay-14.title: Count the sides
arml-2002-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $99$.)* $K=100$, so each square has side $10$. The boundary of $ABCDE$ consists of $10$ square sides on the slanted edges $AB$, $AE$ and $BC$, $DE$ ($4+4+1+1$), together with $CD$, which is $3$ diagonals of squares long, $3\cdot10\sqrt2=30\sqrt2$. The perimeter is $10\cdot10+30\sqrt2=100+30\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $100+30\sqrt2$**

arml-2002-superrelay-15.title: Check the largest candidate
arml-2002-superrelay-15.body:
$99=3\cdot33=10^2-1$ is a two-digit multiple of $3$, and $100$ is already three digits, so no larger two-digit number exists.

**Answer: 99**
